q-161379.name: Question 1
q-161379.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨(x+y)^{2},\,(x-y)^{2},\,xy⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=y-x$ for $-1\le x\le 1$ and $-3\le y\le 0.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{-3}^{0}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?
q-161379.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,v-u⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 1,\,-3\le v\le 0\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨(x+y)^{2},\,(x-y)^{2},\,xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=v-u} \\  & =⟨(u+v)^{2},\,(u-v)^{2},\,uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨(u+v)^{2},\,(u-v)^{2},\,uv⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,-1,\,1⟩ \\  & =(u+v)^{2}\cdot 1+(u-v)^{2}\cdot (-1)+uv\cdot 1 \\  & =5uv.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨(x+y)^{2},\,(x-y)^{2},\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(5uv)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{-3}^{0}5uv\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨(x+y)2,(x−y)2,xy⟩ and the surface S defined by z=y−x for −1≤x≤1 and −3≤y≤0. Using the parametrization x=u and y=v, the flux of F through S can be expressed as ∬SF⋅dS=∫−11∫−30AAAAAAAdvdu. What is the missing expression?

Correct
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

Using the parametrization, where x=u and y=v, our surface can be parameterized as

r(u,v)=⟨u,v,v−u⟩

over the domain

D={(u,v):−1≤u≤1,−3≤v≤0}.

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(u),∂∂u(v),∂∂u(v−u)⟩=⟨1,0,−1⟩rv′=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(u),∂∂v(v),∂∂v(v−u)⟩=⟨0,1,1⟩

Now, the fundamental vector product is

ru′×rv′=|ijk10−1011|=⟨|0−111|,−|1−101|,|1001|⟩=⟨1,−1,1⟩.

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of r(u,v) into F(x,y,z):

F(r(u,v))=⟨(x+y)2,(x−y)2,xy⟩|x=u,y=v,z=v−u=⟨(u+v)2,(u−v)2,uv⟩

Then, we calculate the dot product of F and ru′×rv′:

F(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)=⟨(u+v)2,(u−v)2,uv⟩⋅⟨1,−1,1⟩=(u+v)2⋅1+(u−v)2⋅(−1)+uv⋅1=5uv.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬S⟨(x+y)2,(x−y)2,xy⟩⋅dS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA=∬D(5uv)dA=∫−11∫−305uvdvdu.

q-161381.name: Question 2
q-161381.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z+x,\,y+2z,\,x-4y⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=2x-4y$ for $-2\le x\le 0$ and $-1\le y\le 5.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{-1}^{5}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?
q-161381.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,2u-4v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-2\le u\le 0,\,-1\le v\le 5\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u-4v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u-4v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & -4\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,4,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z+x,\,y+2z,\,x-4y⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=2u-4v} \\  & =⟨2u-4v+u,\,v+2(2u-4v),\,u-4v⟩ \\  & =⟨3u-4v,\,4u-7v,\,u-4v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨3u-4v,\,4u-7v,\,u-4v⟩\cdot ⟨-2,\,4,\,1⟩ \\  & =(3u-4v)\cdot (-2)+(4u-7v)\cdot 4+(u-4v)\cdot 1 \\  & =-6u+8v+16u-28v+u-4v \\  & =11u-24v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z+x,\,y+2z,\,x-4y⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(11u-24v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{-1}^{5}(11u-24v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

q-161358.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z,\,-y,\,2x⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=3x-2y$ for $0\le x\le 5$ and $-3\le y\le 3.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{0}^{5}{\int }_{-3}^{3}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?
q-161358.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,3u-2v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 5,\,-3\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$

$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u+v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 4,\,-2\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u+v} \\  & =⟨u+v-v,\,2v-(u+v),\,uv⟩ \\  & =⟨u,\,v-u,\,uv⟩\end{aligned}

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(uv-v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{-2}^{3}uv-v\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z,\,y+2z,\,2x-y⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=v-u} \\  & =⟨v-u,\,v+2(v-u),\,2u-v⟩ \\  & =⟨v-u,\,3v-2u,\,2u-v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨v-u,\,3v-2u,\,2u-v⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,-1,\,1⟩ \\  & =(v-u)\cdot 1+(3v-2u)\cdot (-1)+(2u-v)\cdot 1 \\  & =v-u-3v+2u+2u-v \\  & =3u-3v.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z,\,y+2z,\,2x-y⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(3u-3v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}(3u-3v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨z,y+2z,2x−y⟩ and the surface S defined by z=y−x for 0≤x≤2 and −1≤y≤2. Using the parametrization x=u and y=v, the flux of F through S can be expressed as ∬SF⋅dS=∫02∫−12AAAAAAAdvdu. What is the missing expression?

a
u+2v
b
2u−3v
c
2u+v
d
3v+u
e
3u−3v
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

Using the parametrization, where x=u and y=v, our surface can be parameterized as

r(u,v)=⟨u,v,v−u⟩

over the domain

D={(u,v):0≤u≤2,−1≤v≤2}.

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(u),∂∂u(v),∂∂u(v−u)⟩=⟨1,0,−1⟩rv′=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(u),∂∂v(v),∂∂v(v−u)⟩=⟨0,1,1⟩

Now, the fundamental vector product is

ru′×rv′=|ijk10−1011|=⟨|0−111|,−|1−101|,|1001|⟩=⟨1,−1,1⟩.

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of r(u,v) into F(x,y,z):

F(r(u,v))=⟨z,y+2z,2x−y⟩|x=u,y=v,z=v−u=⟨v−u,v+2(v−u),2u−v⟩=⟨v−u,3v−2u,2u−v⟩

Then, we calculate the dot product of F and ru′×rv′:

F(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)=⟨v−u,3v−2u,2u−v⟩⋅⟨1,−1,1⟩=(v−u)⋅1+(3v−2u)⋅(−1)+(2u−v)⋅1=v−u−3v+2u+2u−v=3u−3v.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬S⟨z,y+2z,2x−y⟩⋅dS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA=∬D(3u−3v)dA=∫02∫−12(3u−3v)dvdu.

q-161166.problem:
For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}\frac{\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}}+R)\,\text{d}A.
$$

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?
q-161166.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Since our surface $S$ is of the form $z=g(x,y),$ it can be parameterized as

$$
r(x,y)=⟨x,\,y,\,g(x,y)⟩.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′} & =⟨1,\,0,\,\frac{∂g}{∂x}⟩ \\ {r}_{y}^{′} & =⟨0,\,1,\,\frac{∂g}{∂y}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & \frac{∂g}{∂x} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{∂g}{∂y}\end{aligned}|=⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(x,y))\cdot ({r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

q-161166.html:
Question 6
?

For a surface S given by z=g(x,y) for (x,y)∈D, the flux of the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨P,Q,R⟩ over S is given by ∬SF⋅dS=∬D(AA∂x−Q∂gA+R)dA. From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?

a
−P, ∂P, ∂x
b
−P, ∂g, ∂y
c
P, ∂g, ∂y
d
P, ∂g, ∂x
e
−P, ∂g, ∂x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

Since our surface S is of the form z=g(x,y), it can be parameterized as

r(x,y)=⟨x,y,g(x,y)⟩.

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

rx′=⟨1,0,∂g∂x⟩ry′=⟨0,1,∂g∂y⟩

Now, the fundamental vector product is

rx′×ry′=|ijk10∂g∂x01∂g∂y|=⟨−∂g∂x,−∂g∂y,1⟩.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬SF⋅dS=∬DF(r(x,y))⋅(rx′×ry′)dA=∬D⟨P,Q,R⟩⋅⟨−∂g∂x,−∂g∂y,1⟩dA=∬D(−P∂g∂x−Q∂g∂y+R)dA.

q-161456.name: Question 7
q-161456.problem:
For a surface $S$ given by $x=2yz$ for $(y,z)\in D,$ the flux of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(P+\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}\,z+\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}\,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?
q-161456.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Since our surface $S$ is of the form $x=2yz,$ it can be parameterized as

$$
r(y,z)=⟨2yz,\,y,\,z⟩.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{y}^{′} & =⟨2z,\,1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{z}^{′} & =⟨2y,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{y}^{′}\times {r}_{z}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2z & 1 & 0 \\ 2y & 0 & 1\end{aligned}|=⟨1,\,-2z,\,-2y⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(y,z))\cdot ({r}_{y}^{′}\times {r}_{z}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,-2z,\,-2y⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(P+(\,-2Q)\,z+(\,-2R)\,y\,)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

q-161453.name: Question 8
q-161453.problem:
For a surface $S$ given by $y=-{x}^{2}z$ for $(x,z)\in D,$ the flux of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}\,xz+Q+\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}\,{x}^{2})\,\text{d}A.
$$

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?

*Hint: The orientation of $S$ should be chosen such that the unit normal vector has a positive  $j$-component.*
q-161453.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Since our surface $S$ is of the form $y=-{x}^{2}z,$ it can be parameterized as

$$
r(x,z)=⟨x,\,-{x}^{2}z,z⟩.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′} & =⟨1,\,-2xz,\,0⟩ \\ {r}_{z}^{′} & =⟨0,\,-{x}^{2},\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{z}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -2xz & 0 \\ 0 & -{x}^{2} & 1\end{aligned}|=⟨-2xz,\,-1,\,-{x}^{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

However, notice that the $j$-component is negative. Therefore, we select the normal vector that points in the *opposite* direction:

$$
{r}_{z}^{′}\times {r}_{x}^{′}=-{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{z}^{′}=⟨2xz,\,1,\,{x}^{2}⟩
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(x,z))\cdot ({r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{z}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨P,\,Q,R\,⟩\cdot ⟨2xz,\,1,\,{x}^{2}⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2P\,xz+Q+R\,{x}^{2})\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

q-161453.html:
Question 8
?

For a surface S given by y=−x2z for (x,z)∈D, the flux of the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨P,Q,R⟩ over S is given by ∬SF⋅dS=∬D(Axz+Q+Ax2)dA. From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?

Hint: The orientation of S should be chosen such that the unit normal vector has a positive j-component.

a
2P and R
b
−2P and 2R
c
2P and −2R
d
P and R
e
P and −2R
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA. Since our surface S is of the form y=−x2z, it can be parameterized as

r(x,z)=⟨x,−x2z,z⟩.

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

rx′=⟨1,−2xz,0⟩rz′=⟨0,−x2,1⟩

Now, the fundamental vector product is

rx′×rz′=|ijk1−2xz00−x21|=⟨−2xz,−1,−x2⟩.

However, notice that the j-component is negative. Therefore, we select the normal vector that points in the opposite direction:

rz′×rx′=−rx′×rz′=⟨2xz,1,x2⟩

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬SF⋅dS=∬DF(r(x,z))⋅(rx′×rz′)dA=∬D⟨P,Q,R⟩⋅⟨2xz,1,x2⟩dA=∬D(2Pxz+Q+Rx2)dA.

q-161189.name: Question 9
q-161189.problem:
For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}\frac{∂g}{∂x}+\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\,\text{d}A.
$$

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?
q-161189.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Since our surface $S$ is of the form $z=g(x,y),$ it can be parameterized as

$$
r(x,y)=⟨x,\,y,\,g(x,y)⟩.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′} & =⟨1,\,0,\,\frac{∂g}{∂x}⟩ \\ {r}_{y}^{′} & =⟨0,\,1,\,\frac{∂g}{∂y}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & \frac{∂g}{∂x} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{∂g}{∂y}\end{aligned}|=⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(x,y))\cdot ({r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}+(-Q\,)\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

q-161457.html:
Question 10
?

For a surface S given by z=g(x,y) for (x,y)∈D, the flux of the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨P,Q,R⟩ over S is given by ∬SF⋅dS=∬D(−PA∂x−A∂gA+R)dA. From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?

a
∂g, −Q, ∂Q
b
∂g, Q, ∂z
c
∂g, −Q, ∂y
d
∂g, Q, ∂y
e
∂g, −Q, ∂z
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

Since our surface S is of the form z=g(x,y), it can be parameterized as

r(x,y)=⟨x,y,g(x,y)⟩.

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

rx′=⟨1,0,∂g∂x⟩ry′=⟨0,1,∂g∂y⟩

Now, the fundamental vector product is

rx′×ry′=|ijk10∂g∂x01∂g∂y|=⟨−∂g∂x,−∂g∂y,1⟩.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬SF⋅dS=∬DF(r(x,y))⋅(rx′×ry′)dA=∬D⟨P,Q,R⟩⋅⟨−∂g∂x,−∂g∂y,1⟩dA=∬D(−P∂g∂x−Q∂g∂y+R)dA.

q-161553.name: Question 11
q-161553.problem:
Calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨{e}^{x},\,{e}^{y},\,z+1⟩,
$$

where the surface $S$ is defined by $z=-x-y$ for $0\le x\le 1$ and $0\le y\le 1.$
q-161553.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the partial derivatives of the graph $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-x-y)=-1 \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-x-y)=-1\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the flux of $F$ through $S$ is given by 

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨{e}^{x},\,{e}^{y},\,z+1⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

Next, we substitute the equation $z=g(x,y)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y,g(x,y)) & =⟨{e}^{x},\,{e}^{y},\,z+1⟩{|}_{z=-x-y} \\  & =⟨{{{e}^{x}}_{⏟}}_{P},\,{{{e}^{y}}_{⏟}}_{Q},\,{{1-x-y}_{⏟}}_{R}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can evaluate our surface integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨{e}^{x},\,{e}^{y},\,z+1⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-({e}^{x})\cdot (-1)-({e}^{y})\cdot (-1)+1-x-y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}({e}^{x}+{e}^{y}+1-x-y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{x}+{e}^{y}+1-x-y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[{e}^{x}y+{e}^{y}+y-xy-\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{x}+e+1-x-\frac{1}{2}-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{x}-x-\frac{1}{2}+e)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[{e}^{x}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-\frac{x}{2}+ex]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =e-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}+e-1 \\  & =2e-2\end{aligned}
$$

∬SF⋅dS=∬D(−P∂g∂x−Q∂g∂y+R)dA.

F(x,y,g(x,y))=⟨ex,ey,z+1⟩|z=−x−y=⟨ex⏟P,ey⏟Q,1−x−y⏟R⟩

Therefore, we can evaluate our surface integral as follows:

q-161541.name: Question 12
q-161541.problem:
Calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
F(x,y,z)=⟨\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,{z}^{2}+1⟩,
$$

where the surface $S$ is defined by $z=2\sqrt{xy}$ for $3\le x\le 4$ and $1\le y\le 2.$
q-161541.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the partial derivatives of the graph $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2\sqrt{xy})=\sqrt{\frac{y}{x}} \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2\sqrt{xy})=\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the flux of $F$ through $S$ is given by 

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,{z}^{2}+1⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

Next, we substitute the equation $z=g(x,y)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y,g(x,y)) & =⟨\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,{z}^{2}+1⟩{|}_{z=2\sqrt{xy}} \\  & =⟨{{\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}}_{⏟}}_{P},\,{{\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}}_{⏟}}_{Q},\,{{4xy+1}_{⏟}}_{R}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can evaluate our surface integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}},\,{z}^{2}+1⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}\cdot \sqrt{\frac{y}{x}}-\sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}\cdot \sqrt{\frac{x}{y}}+4xy+1)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-1-\frac{x}{y}+4xy+1)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-\frac{x}{y}+4xy)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{4}{\int }_{1}^{2}(-\frac{x}{y}+4xy)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{4}{[-x\operatorname{ln}⁡y+2x{y}^{2}]}_{y=1}^{y=2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{4}(-x\operatorname{ln}⁡2+8x+0-2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{3}^{4}(6-\operatorname{ln}⁡2)x\,\text{d}x \\  & =(6-\operatorname{ln}⁡2){[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{3}^{4} \\  & =\frac{7(6-\operatorname{ln}⁡2)}{2}\end{aligned}

q-161476.problem:
Evaluate the surface integral

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨\frac{1}{z},\,\frac{xy}{z},\,z⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

where the surface $S$ is defined by $z={e}^{x-y}$ for $0\le x\le 1$ and $0\le y\le x.$
q-161476.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the partial derivatives of the graph $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}{e}^{x-y}={e}^{x-y} \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}{e}^{x-y}=-{e}^{x-y}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the equation $z=g(x,y)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y,g(x,y)) & =⟨\frac{1}{z},\,\frac{xy}{z},\,z⟩{|}_{z={e}^{x-y}} \\  & =⟨{e}^{-(x-y)},\,xy{e}^{-(x-y)},\,{e}^{x-y}⟩ \\  & =⟨{{{e}^{y-x}}_{⏟}}_{P},\,{{xy{e}^{y-x}}_{⏟}}_{Q},\,{{{e}^{x-y}}_{⏟}}_{R}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can evaluate our surface integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨\frac{1}{z},\,\frac{xy}{z},\,z⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-{e}^{y-x}\cdot {e}^{x-y}-(xy{e}^{y-x})\cdot (-{e}^{x-y})+{e}^{x-y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-1+xy+{e}^{x-y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}(-1+xy+{e}^{x-y})\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[-y+\frac{x{y}^{2}}{2}-{e}^{x-y}]}_{y=0}^{y=x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(-x+\frac{{x}^{3}}{2}-1+{e}^{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{8}-x+{e}^{x}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{8}-1+e)-1 \\  & =-\frac{19}{8}+e\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨y,\,x+z,\,z+2x⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

where the surface $S$ is defined by $z=y-2x$ for $1\le x\le 2$ and $0\le y\le 1.$
q-161447.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y-2x)=-2 \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y-2x)=1\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the equation $z=g(x,y)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y,g(x,y)) & =⟨y,\,x+z,\,z+2x⟩{|}_{z=y-2x} \\  & =⟨y,\,x+(y-2x),\,y-2x+2x⟩ \\  & =⟨{{y}_{⏟}}_{P},\,{{y-x}_{⏟}}_{Q},\,{{y}_{⏟}}_{R}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can evaluate our surface integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨y,\,x+z,\,z+2x⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-y\cdot (-2)-(y-x)\cdot (1)+y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2y-y+x+y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(2y+x)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(2y+x)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{[{y}^{2}+xy]}_{y=0}^{y=1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}(1+x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[x+\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =2+2-1-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate the surface integral

$$
{∬}_{S}⟨z+y,\,2y+z,\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S
$$

where the surface $S$ is defined by $z=x-y$ for $0\le x\le 1$ and $0\le y\le 2.$
q-160888.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x-y)=1 \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x-y)=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the equation $z=g(x,y)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x,y,g(x,y)) & =⟨z+y,\,2y+z,\,xy⟩{|}_{z=x-y} \\  & =⟨(x-y)+y,\,2y+(x-y),\,xy⟩ \\  & =⟨{{x}_{⏟}}_{P},\,{{x+y}_{⏟}}_{Q},\,{{xy}_{⏟}}_{R}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can evaluate our surface integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z+y,\,2y+z,\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-(x)\cdot 1-(x+y)\cdot (-1)+xy)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-x+x+y+xy)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(y+xy)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}(y+xy)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}x{y}^{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(2+2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =[2x+{x}^{2}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =(2(1)+{1}^{2})-0 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
